crop.notes: Clipping is the continuation of 'Expressions of the Sports' (part of 'Stirring Scenes in St. Louis'); it starts mid-list ('...Grounds Association') and the headline and opening are in the column to the left. The Allen mention, in Al Spink's diagnosis (crop-4), is complete.

ocr.notes: Mostly right, with scattered errors (e.g. 'Sepppaced', 'ig, eagle', 'idea < blow'). The Allen sentence is transcribed correctly.

title.suggested: Al Spink Recalls Tom Allen at the Sullivan-Kilrain Fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat printed St. Louis sporting men's views on Fitzsimmons' win over Corbett. Al Spink recalled Tom Allen at ringside at the Sullivan-Kilrain fight at Richburg saying, "They fight like a pair of old wash women."

metadata.notes: Masthead reads St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Thursday Morning, March 18, 1897, page 4.

facts.fact: Allen was at ringside for the bare-knuckle Sullivan-Kilrain fight at Richburg
At the Sullivan-Kilrain fight Allen said of the two fighters that they fought like a pair of old wash women
facts.quote: They fight like a pair of old wash women.

notes: The current summary is wrong: Allen was not quoted about the Corbett-Fitzsimmons fight and nothing about bare hands without gloves or play acting appears. His only mention is Al Spink's recollection of him at the 1889 Sullivan-Kilrain fight; facts are medium because they are Spink's secondhand memory. Fight date is from the known Sullivan-Kilrain bout, not stated in the article.
